headline: TAXUD’s 5 October guidance: UK e-commerce sellers must send EAN product identifiers to EU customs from 1 November
executive_summary: This Monday-to-Monday week has one identification keep, and it is an EU customs data duty that binds UK exporters, not a UK statute. On 5 October the Commission’s TAXUD directorate published a revised ‘Guidance for Member States and Trade’ on the temporary EUR 3 customs duty. Section 8 now says that from 1 November 2026 every distance-sale import of goods with an intrinsic value not exceeding EUR 150 must carry product identifiers on the customs declaration: a merchant identifier, a manufacturer identifier, and, where it exists, a standardised identifier. The guidance names EAN as the usual standardised identifier and says it is typically encoded in EAN-13 or UPC barcodes, QR codes or RFID. It is not a GS1 legal mandate: where no standardised identifier exists the declarant uses code Y081, and the Commission is still amending Annex B to lock the EUR 150 cap into the legal text. Dutch Customs published a member-state how-to on 8 October using the same C127, C128, C129 and Y081 codes. Last week’s Exchange for Change registration and PET/metal transition notes are not repeated. Construction and healthcare produced no new identifier, data-carrier or registry instrument. SI 2026/1053 still comes into force on 17 October.
cross_sector_themes: The live identifier clock this week is an EU customs data element, not a UK barcode reprint – GTIN already on the pack must now travel with the declaration
EAN is named as the usual standardised product identifier; GS1 is not mandated and Y081 remains the lawful absence code
The Commission says it is amending Annex B to limit the PID duty to consignments of EUR 150 or less; that cap is in the 5 October guidance, not yet a finished legal amendment
UK statute and scheme files (DRS testing guidelines, GB UDI, construction-product library, EN 18239/18246 citation) did not move

sector_overviews.headline: EU customs will demand EAN product identifiers on low-value e-commerce imports from 1 November; DRS barcodes did not move
sector_overviews.summary: Retail’s keep is the 5 October TAXUD guidance, restated operationally by Dutch Customs on 8 October. UK retailers, brands and marketplaces that sell to EU consumers while the goods are still outside the Union must get three identifiers to the customs declarant: the shop or platform SKU (M-PID), the manufacturer’s internal code (NS-PID), and the EAN/GTIN or ISBN where one exists (S-PID). Enforcement starts on 1 November, twenty days from this digest. The EUR 3 duty itself has applied since 1 July; this week’s text is the product-identifier chapter, including a stated intention to confine it to consignments of EUR 150 or less. Exchange for Change published nothing after 30 September. Product-testing guidelines promised by September are still ‘in due course’, and the certified reverse-vending-machine list is still indicated for October and is not on the news page. The toys-safety call for evidence closed at 23:59 on 6 October with no summary of responses. PackUK’s 8 October collection update is a PRN/PERN reprocessor guide, not 2026/27 fees.

sector_overviews.headline: No new construction-product identifier, library or GSR text; BSR’s October data are Gateway 2 volumes
sector_overviews.summary: MHCLG, OPSS and the Building Safety Regulator published no new unique-identifier, digital-product-record or golden-thread product-data instrument this week. The Building Safety Regulator’s 6–9 October statistics cover Gateway 2 application volumes in July–September 2026 and attribute a September rise to filings ahead of the building safety levy; they do not change how products are identified. A 5 October Building magazine think-tank on Gateway 3 restates existing golden-thread practice and does not create an identifier duty. The Manufacturers’ Information Hub remains at proof-of-concept complete / MVP in development. Government responses to the Construction Products Reform White Paper and the General Safety Requirement consultation are still indicated later in 2026. Official Journal citation of EN 18239 and EN 18246 has still not appeared. Construction exporters of batteries, or of products incorporating them, still sit on SI 2026/1053 from 17 October and the 18 February 2027 QR-code and passport clocks.

sector_overviews.headline: No new Scan4Safety, GB UDI or medicines-packaging instrument; TAXUD treats UDI-DI as the S-PID for EU D2C device parcels
sector_overviews.summary: Healthcare has no standalone keep this week. The 5 October TAXUD guidance is primarily a retail/e-commerce file, but section 8.8 says that where a UDI-DI exists under the EU MDR or IVDR it is deemed the standardised product identifier for low-value distance-sale imports, and that the GS1 application identifier 01 (the GTIN in a medicines DataMatrix) may be used as S-PID for medicinal products. That matters only to UK device and medicines sellers shipping direct to EU consumers; it is not a GB UDI instrument. The government’s 6 October response to the National Commission on AI in healthcare, and the opening of MHRA AI Airlock Phase 3, are lifecycle and post-market-surveillance policy for software devices and do not create a UDI, implant-card, MDOR or pack-DataMatrix duty. Scan4Safety’s site has no dated 5–12 October post; the 17 September GS1 UK / PSC report is not repeated. Draft Medical Devices (Amendment) Regulations 2026 remain the December file, with GB UDI still indicated to enter into force in June 2027.

items.title: TAXUD 5 October guidance: EAN identifiers mandatory on EU e-commerce imports from 1 November
items.summary: On 5 October 2026 DG TAXUD issued a revised Guidance for Member States and Trade on the temporary EUR 3 customs duty. From 1 November 2026, distance-sale imports of goods in consignments of EUR 150 or less must carry a merchant product identifier, a manufacturer identifier and, where it exists, a standardised identifier such as an EAN. The guidance is not a GS1 mandate: if no standardised identifier exists the declarant uses code Y081. Dutch Customs published a matching how-to on 8 October.
items.what_changed:
The Commission’s Directorate-General for Taxation and Customs Union published ‘The temporary EUR 3 customs duty and the Union handling fee – Guidance for Member States and Trade’, version of 5 October 2026, replacing the 2 June 2026 text at the same official download URL. Section 8 is the identification file. It says the new product-identifier requirement applies to all goods sold in distance sales of imported goods with an intrinsic value not exceeding EUR 150 from 1 November 2026. Voluntary submission ran from 1 July; ‘effective enforcement starts from 1 November 2026’. The Commission ‘is in the process of amending Annex B’ of the UCC Delegated Act to clarify that the duty is limited to those low-value consignments. B2B flows are in principle out of scope.

Three identifiers must be provided or made available to customs. C127 is the merchant product identifier assigned by the online seller, marketplace or platform, unique on that site for the exact product offered. C128 is the non-standardised manufacturer identifier; if none exists the manufacturer is expected to assign one, and may use the standardised identifier for this field as well. C129 is the standardised manufacturer identifier ‘only where it exists’. TAXUD writes that in Europe the most common S-PID are ‘the EAN (European Article Number) for many products and the ISBN … for books’, usually encoded in barcodes (EAN-13, UPC), QR codes or RFID. There is ‘no obligation to assign S-PID to all products’; where none has been assigned the exception code Y081 is declared. Using a batch- or unit-level code where a model-level identifier exists is treated as an infringement. For healthcare, a UDI-DI under the EU MDR or IVDR is deemed an S-PID, and the medicines product code (GS1 AI 01) may be used as S-PID. On 8 October Dutch Customs published a member-state page repeating the 1 November start, the F48/F49/F53 declaration types, and the C127/C128/C129/Y081 codes, and linking this same TAXUD PDF.
items.why_it_matters_to_gs1:
This is a customs data-carrier and unique-identifier duty on UK-to-EU business-to-consumer e-commerce, twenty days from enforcement. GS1 is not named and is not mandated. TAXUD’s standardised identifier is an internationally recognised number that already exists; for almost every GS1 UK retail member that number is the GTIN encoded in an EAN-13 or UPC. Members who treat ‘no barcode on the web listing’ as ‘no S-PID’ while an EAN exists in My Numberbank or on the pack will mis-declare Y081. Members who invent a new proprietary code instead of sending the GTIN they already scan at UK POS will give EU customs a number that cannot be matched to recalled or non-compliant SKUs – the opposite of the stated control objective.

Two traps sit in this week’s text. First, the EUR 150 cap is in the 5 October guidance and is described as an Annex B amendment still in process. UK advisers who read only the June legal text of Delegated Regulation (EU) 2026/1022 will keep preparing for all distance-sale values; those who read only the new guidance may wrongly drop SKUs above EUR 150 before the amendment is adopted. Second, the manufacturer may lawfully reuse the GTIN as the NS-PID (C128 and C129 the same). That is an opportunity for GS1 UK to show members a clean mapping – GLN for the seller/declarant location, GTIN for C129 and optionally C128, shop SKU for C127 – without claiming a mandate. If GS1 UK does nothing, carriers and IOSS holders will specify proprietary item codes while members already hold GTINs for GDSN, Sunrise 2027 and DRS. If members do nothing, 1 November arrives with listings that cannot be declared, parcels held, and a Y081 habit that throws away the one identifier EU customs can actually verify on the pack. Device and medicines sellers shipping direct to EU consumers should map UDI-DI or AI 01 into the same C129 field rather than inventing a second number.
gs1_standards_implicated: GTIN as the usual S-PID (TAXUD names EAN; EAN-13 / UPC-A / UPC-E encode the GTIN)

UDI-DI (often a GTIN) as S-PID for EU MDR/IVDR devices sold D2C into the Union

next_steps.action: If you sell B2C into the EU from GB stock, map every in-scope SKU to three fields before 1 November: shop/platform SKU (C127), manufacturer code (C128), and existing GTIN/EAN/ISBN (C129); use Y081 only where no standardised identifier exists, and test a live declaration with your carrier

Issue a short exporter note that translates TAXUD’s EAN/S-PID language into GTIN, states plainly that GS1 is not mandated, and warns against declaring Y081 when a GTIN already exists on pack or in My Numberbank
Ask brand owners whether they will reuse the GTIN as NS-PID (C128 = C129), which TAXUD expressly allows, so the customs file is not a third proprietary code
Offer IOSS holders and major carriers a one-page GTIN-to-C129 mapping, including the healthcare UDI-DI and AI 01 tolerances, without claiming a GS1 legal mandate
Watch the promised Annex B amendment that would confine the PID duty to consignments of EUR 150 or less; until it is adopted, do not treat the cap as finished law
